newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BLOW AHEAD OF FRENCH TITLE DEFENCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV BLOW AHEAD OF FRENCH TITLE DEFENCE.

text.p: World number three Yevgeny Kafelnikov suffered a blow ahead of his French Open title defence when he crashed out in the first round of the Grand Prix event on Tuesday.
Second seed Kafelnikov, who was sidelined for three months with a broken finger in his right hand, lasted less than an hour against unfancied Slovak Dominik Hrbaty, losing 6-3 6-3.
The Russian had appeared to be improving steadily when he made it to the quarter-finals of last week's Italian Open and the Hamburg semi-finals.
Earlier on Tuesday, third-seeded Chilean Marcelo Rios, who won last year's title, had difficulties getting past Italian Andrea Gaudenzi 6-4 4-6 6-4.
"The court is lot faster here than in Rome. I would like to win this tournament again," said Rios, a finalist in Rome and winner in Monte Carlo this year.
Switzerland's Olympic champion and fifth seed Marc Rosset also struggled before beating Armenia's Sargis Sargsian 6-2 4-6 7-6 (7-2).
Kafelnikov is the fourth seed failing to make the second round. Eighth-seeded Swede Thomas Johansson lost to Austria's Gilbert Schaller 4-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-6 (7-4) on Tuesday.
On Monday, fourth-seeded Briton Tim Henman and sixth-seeded Swede Jonas Bjoerkman were knocked out by Dutchman Sjeng Schalken and Austrian Clemens Trimmel respectively.
